title: Tesla Stock News (Oct 16, 2026): TSLA Falls 1.3% to $362.44
summary: Tesla (TSLA) fell 1.29% to $362.44 on Oct 15 as reports said energy chief Mike Snyder is leaving, ahead of the Roadster reveal.
body_markdown:
## Why Tesla Stock Fell


No fetched source named a company-specific reason for the session's drop, so the move is best read against a mixed market in which some large tech stocks also slipped. Three Tesla stories framed the day.


As reported by[Stocktwits](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/tesla-energy-chief-mike-snyder-231825246.html) , citing The Wall Street Journal, Mike Snyder, Tesla's vice president of energy and charging, is leaving, with AJ Booth, senior director of energy products engineering, reportedly replacing him. Snyder has not announced the exit publicly, and the report links it to Elon Musk's push toward AI and robotics.


According to[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/teslas-roadster-event-is-on-tonight-heres-what-to-expect-000407218.html) , Tesla staged its Roadster reveal at SpaceX's facility in Waco, Texas, after pushing it back two weeks from October 1, citing weather at the demo site. Musk said, "We enter production in 2028."


Per[Axios](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/ai-could-drive-tesla-spacex-213713674.html) , Barclays analysts led by Dan Levy wrote that a Tesla-SpaceX merger "could come as soon as this fall," though shareholders would still need to approve any deal.


## TSLA Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Stocktwits reported that Tesla deployed 13.7 GWh of storage products, up from 12.5 GWh a year earlier, and that a new Megapack factory in Texas began production in August.
- Yahoo Finance reported that Tesla measured 0 to 60 mph in 0.81 seconds during a Roadster test at the event, with all three versions claiming a range above 300 miles.
- The stock closed $7.21 above its day low on volume 26.90% below average.


### Risks


- The energy business loses its leader while, per Stocktwits, energy generation and storage made up about 13.5% of 2025 revenue.
- Roadster production is not slated until 2028, and Deepwater Management's Gene Munster called the event "an engineering flex with no commercial value beyond embarrassing traditional car makers," according to Yahoo Finance.
- Axios noted significant downside risks to a Tesla-SpaceX deal, which would need shareholder approval.


Axios reported that Tesla's annual shareholder meeting could be held no later than December 6.
